heading: CHAPTER XXIII.
title: HOW FLATTERERS SHOULD BE AVOIDED
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 23 says the danger of flatterers cannot be solved by either total openness or total secrecy. A wise prince creates a narrow truth regime: selected counsellors, invited truth, wide inquiry, and final judgment kept in the prince's own hands.
The Maximilian example shows the opposite failure. Secrecy without disciplined counsel leaves the prince pliant, obstructed, and impossible to rely on.
The chapter ends by reversing a common assumption. Good counsels come from the prince's wisdom, because only a wise prince can choose, question, control, and unite counsel without being ruled by it.
